body: Across this library, edges fall into two buckets. Structural (not copyable): scale and leverage across asset classes (Soros, Druckenmiller), proprietary data/compute/scientists and capacity caps (Simons' Medallion: 39% net 1988-2018, while Renaissance's public funds did far worse), activism and board influence (Ackman), locked-up distressed capital (Marks, Klarman), pre-IPO/block access and network (Indian superstars). Process (largely copyable): Kelly-style sizing (Thorp), downside-first margin of safety (Klarman), special situations driven by non-economic selling (Greenblatt), three-legged stool / scale-economies-shared quality tests (Akre, Sleep, Smith), capital-cycle supply analysis (Andrade), valuation-based allocation (Naren, Jain), avoid-lists and loser-cutting (Arora), scuttlebutt (Fisher), inversion and bias checklists (Munger), cycle temperature (Marks, Templeton). Small size is the individual's one structural advantage: positions in micro/small caps and special situations too small for funds (Greenblatt and Buffett both credit small size early). Common failures across greats: concentration in a broken thesis (Valeant, Horsehead), buying a mania late (Druckenmiller 2000), style droughts of 5+ years (Fundsmith 2021-25, Baupost post-2014, Jain 2018-20). Implication: copy processes, accept multi-year underperformance as normal, and never copy leverage.

title: Investor edges: structural vs process, and what an individual can copy
